main_text.p: at electos Dei condemnare? Siquidem ipse Christus, qui judex omnium a Deo constitutus est, mortem pro illis obiit, nec tantum ipsorum causâ mortuus est, verum etiam a mortuis excitatus, in cœlum ascendit, ibique ad dextram Dei evectus, summam potestatem in cœlo & terra obtinuit; denique quod fidum & misericordem Pontificem decet, continenter apud Deum pro nobis intercedit, nosque suo favore & præsidio perpetuo protegit.

Observa & hoc, causam, quæ Deum Judicem movet, ut nos justificet, est Mors Christi, quatenus per illâ satisfactū est justitiæ ipsius pro nobis. Quod autem per mortem divinæ justitiæ plenè satisfactum sit, & peccata nostra perfectè expiata, demonstrant hic, tum Resurrectio Christi ex morte, tum Ascensio ejusdem in cœlum, & Sessio ad dexteram Dei Patris. Neq; enim ex morte ad vitam illam cœlestem ac gloriosam resurgere potuisset, nisi ꝑ peccatis nostris, quæ ut Sponsor in se susceperat, plenè satisfecisset. Unde 1,

page.notes: Catchword "Cor," is at the lower right. The page number is printed at the top left in an ornamental form; "142" is my reading and is uncertain. "at electos" at the start of the page is read as "at", a fragment of the previous page's sentence. Printed "ꝑ" is read as per. "illâ" and "satisfactū" are copied with their printed marks, which I could not check closely at this resolution. No signature visible.
